For the duplicated entity invariants, the direction of consolidation is an ownership decision between the cobre-core and cobre-io owners: delete the unreachable builder copies, or make cobre-core the single owner and have cobre-io delegate — this envelope evidences the duplication but does not pick.

Whether the generic-constraint-bounds duplicate-key rule is intentionally stricter than the six-family rule (per row rather than per column) or is an unnoticed divergence needs the rule's author; the two doc comments each assert their own semantics without acknowledging the other.

Whether any of these setup-time validation costs clears the project's bar for action is an owner call, since the standing rule accepts setup-time recomputation and none of these paths has been measured on a fixed deck.

If the per-stage raw column count gets a single owner, the owner must decide whether it belongs beside the stage-id resolver, which both consumers already share, or stays inside the validation layer as a value passed between the two semantic modules.

Both entry-point crates pin `cobre-io` with `features = ["schema"]` and every CI job lists `schema` in NON_SOLVER_FEATURES, so no build in the repo ever compiles the off-state of the 129-site feature gate; whether that optional-dependency seam still earns its keep is an owner call, because cobre-io is a published crate whose external consumers are not visible from here.

evidence.reading: Five config admission rules — historical-scheme restricted to the inflow class, seed required once any class leaves in-sample, `openings` only under `training`, historical year range ordered, `historical_years` only with a historical class — live in `validate_scenario_source_cfg` / `validate_openings_cfg`, whose only caller is `convert_scenario_source_config` at :227-228, itself reachable only from the two `Config::*_scenario_source` accessors. The Layer-2 gate `validate_config` checks exactly two other things and never resolves a scenario source, so the comment at scenarios.rs:459 asserting these reads cannot fail is not underwritten by anything. Every one of the nine cobre-io call sites discards the error with a let-else return or `.ok()`. The consequence is inverted enforcement: an invalid scenario-source config does not fail the load, it silently switches off the rules that read it — `check_external_scheme_has_files` returns before doing any work rather than reporting either the config defect or the missing external files. candidates.fixShape: Move the admission decision to the point where the config is admitted, not to whoever happens to read it. Resolve both scenario sources once inside the Layer-2 config gate, report their failures into the validation context alongside every other layer's findings, and hand the already-resolved values to the semantic rules so those rules take a resolved value rather than a fallible accessor. The accessors then become infallible reads of an already-admitted config and the nine let-else arms disappear with the fallibility that motivated them. This is the 0a admission gate applied to the block that exists today: an unsupported combination becomes a rejection, never a silent ignore. Distinct from the registered three-representation item — nothing here is about Config versus the downstream params projections, only about where Config's own rules are enforced.
candidates.title: The config admission rules are enforced only as a side effect of an accessor, and every cobre-io caller discards the resulting error on a premise the Layer-2 gate does not satisfy

evidence.command: sed -n '846,857p' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/semantic/scenarios.rs
evidence.reading: The comparison depends only on the class, the two column indices `cn` and `cm`, and the source stage depth `sn`; nothing inside the three nested loops reads the edge itself except the message text. The `for s in 0..=sn` loop restarts at stage 0 for every transition, and the inner `entities.iter().find_map` does two hash lookups per entity at every stage. A column pair that recurs on several edges of the declared graph therefore has its whole shared prefix re-compared once per edge.

candidates.fixShape: Compare each distinct column pair once rather than once per edge. Collect the distinct pairs with their maximum source stage depth and one representative edge before the comparison, then walk each pair's prefix a single time and attribute the first disagreement to its representative edge. The warnings emitted stay the same in content and in count per pair, and the trunk is walked once per pair instead of once per edge. If per-edge attribution must be preserved exactly, keep the per-edge loop but short-circuit on a pair already decided.
candidates.mechanism: Redundant repeated pass. The cost is the sum over edges of the source stage depth times the entity count times two hash lookups, so it grows with the product of the edge count, the horizon length and the entity count for a rule that only ever emits a warning. Because the comparison is a pure function of the column pair and the deepest source stage at which it appears, every extra edge carrying an already-compared pair is repeated work. The path is setup-time, once per case load, and only fires when the stage file declares an explicit node list.
candidates.title: Prefix-coherence re-walks the entire root prefix for every graph edge, so a repeated column pair is compared once per edge instead of once per pair

evidence.command: grep -n 'let mut cells\|let mut entity_scen\|let mut union_by_stage\|let mut inflow_sample_rows\|inflow_sample_rows.push\|class.cells.get\|policy_graph.nodes.is_empty()' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/semantic/scenarios.rs
evidence.reading: Every external row drives four inserts inside the single row loop: a `cells` hash insert (line 665), a `union_by_stage` set insert (line 684), an `entity_scen` set insert (lines 685-688), and, for the inflow class, a full row copy pushed onto `inflow_sample_rows` (line 694). Three of the four are index views of the same (stage, scenario, entity) triples. The only reader of `cells` values is `check_prefix_coherence` at line 855, and line 620 shows that call is guarded by a non-empty declared node list, so on a chain-dialect deck the values are built and dropped unread; the map's remaining duty there is duplicate-key detection, which needs the keys only. Line 2745 confirms the chain fixture is a first-class shape in this module's own tests.

candidates.fixShape: Build only what a rule will read. On a deck with no declared node list the class extraction can carry a key-only set for duplicate detection and skip the values entirely, since the value-carrying map has no other reader. The per-stage scenario-id union is derivable from the per-(stage, entity) sets already built and need not be a third copy. The inflow row copy can go away by widening the moment reduction to accept an iterator, or by feeding it the triple-keyed map directly, which removes a full duplicate of the largest external table. For the inflow class the largest external table is materialized roughly four times over during validation: a hash map keyed by the triple with an f64 payload, a per-stage ordered set of scenario ids, a per-(stage, entity) ordered set of scenario ids, and a verbatim row copy. The row copy exists because the moment reduction takes a slice rather than an iterator. Peak resident memory during validation therefore scales as a multiple of the biggest input file, and each row pays several separate container insertions. The path is setup-time, once per case load, on rank 0.
candidates.title: `extract_class` materializes four full-table-sized structures per external class, one of which carries values no rule reads on the chain dialect
